1.title: Tears turned into prayer
1.text: On hearing of Jerusalem's ruin, Nehemiah does not act at once: he sits down, weeps, and fasts and prays before the God of heaven. The rebuilding begins on his knees.

1.question: What does Nehemiah do as he prays for the children of Israel?
options: Confesses Israel's sins, including his own
Asks for vengeance against the enemies who oppress Judah's people
Demands that the king grant him an army to free Judah
Blames only the other nations for Israel's sins

1.question: What position did Nehemiah hold with the king?
options: The king's cupbearer
Captain of the army
High priest
Scribe of the law

2.title: A silent prayer
2.text: When the king asks, Nehemiah prays to the God of heaven before answering. It is an instant prayer, in the middle of the conversation, showing how he depended on God at every step.

2.question: What did the king grant Nehemiah concerning the journey?
options: To send him, with a set time appointed
Refused the request and kept him in Susa
Granted him the position of governor at once
Sent soldiers without giving any answer

2.question: How did Sanballat and Tobiah react to Nehemiah's coming?
options: It grieved them that someone sought Israel's welfare
They rejoiced greatly and offered support for the rebuilding
They sent letters to the king asking for more soldiers
They did not notice Nehemiah's arrival in Jerusalem

2.question: What did Nehemiah do by night as he went up by the brook?
options: He viewed the wall and turned back
He gathered the people to begin the work at once
He confronted the guards watching the wall
He ran back in fear of the enemies

2.question: What did Nehemiah answer those who mocked?
options: The God of heaven will prosper us
We will tell Sanballat that he is mistaken about us
We will call the king's army to defend us
We will invite you to help with the rebuilding

3.title: The sheep gate
3.text: The rebuilding begins at the sheep gate, built by the high priest Eliashib and his brethren the priests. They sanctified it, recalling that the work of the wall was also a sacred act.

3.question: What did the nobles of the Tekoites do?
options: They put not their necks to the work of their Lord
They repaired two large sections of the wall with their brethren
They alone built the tower of Hananeel and of Meah
They guarded the city gates throughout the whole night

3.question: Where did Jedaiah the son of Harumaph repair the wall?
options: Over against his own house
By the tower of the furnaces
At the valley gate
By the king's garden

3.question: Who repaired the gate of the fountain?
options: Shallun the son of Col-hozeh, ruler of Mizpah
Meremoth the son of Urijah, ruler of the region of Tekoa
Zadok the son of Baana, ruler of the neighboring district
Hanun the son of Zalaph, leader of the men of Zanoah

3.question: What stands out in the work of Baruch the son of Zabbai?
options: He earnestly repaired another piece
He refused to help until he was paid for the work
He repaired only the tower of the furnaces with his sons
He kept watch at the east gate throughout the night

3.question: What did Palal the son of Uzai repair?
options: The tower by the king's high house, near the prison court
The wall of the pool of Siloah, near the king's garden, unto the stairs
The fish gate together with its locks and its bronze bars
The tower of Hananeel next to the old tower of Meah

3.question: Who repaired between the corner and the sheep gate?
options: The goldsmiths and the merchants
The priests who served daily in the temple
The Levites in charge of songs and offerings
The nobles of Tekoa and their servants

4.title: Tobiah's mockery
4.text: Tobiah the Ammonite scoffs that even a fox would break down that stone wall. The enemies' contempt is a weapon as real as the sword.

4.question: How did Nehemiah respond to the mockery of Sanballat and Tobiah?
options: By praying to God against them
By attacking them at once
By stopping the work on the wall
By sending them gifts

4.question: What did Judah say while they built?
options: The strength of the bearers is decayed and there is much rubbish
The enemies are far too many for us to overcome them by ourselves
The wall has many breaches and we will not have time to repair them all
There are no more stones left to finish building the wall

4.question: How were Nehemiah's servants organized from that day on?
options: Half worked and half held the weapons
They all left the work and fled to their homes in fear
They all took up weapons and abandoned the wall's building
They went home to sleep as they had done before

4.question: What did Nehemiah and his men do with their clothes?
options: They did not take them off; each kept his weapon
They changed them every night before sleeping on the wall
They wore golden armor given by the king
They left them stored near the gate

5.title: Against usury
5.text: Nehemiah considers it in his heart and then rebukes the nobles for exacting usury from their own brethren. Justice within the people matters as much as the wall without.

5.question: What was the people's complaint against their brethren?
options: They brought sons and daughters into bondage for debt
They refused to build the wall together with their brethren
They secretly worshipped idols of the neighboring nations
They abandoned Jerusalem because of the famine

5.question: What did Nehemiah propose about the loans?
options: To leave off this usury
To charge even higher interest on the poor
To sell the debtors to neighboring nations
To seize their lands as payment

5.question: Why did Nehemiah not oppress the people like the former governors?
options: Because of the fear of God
Because the king forbade it
Because he was already very rich
Because the people threatened him

5.question: What is Nehemiah's request to God at the end of the chapter?
options: Think upon me, my God, for good
Destroy all my enemies and their descendants
Give me more riches than my brethren
Make me king over all the people of Judah

6.title: Fifty-two days
6.text: Despite all the threats and intrigue, the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth of Elul, in just fifty-two days. The enemies recognized that the work had been done by the God of Israel.

6.question: How many times did the enemies summon Nehemiah to meet?
options: Four times, and he answered the same way
Seven times, and he finally went to meet them
Five times, and he went to meet them in the valley of Ono
Two times, and he ignored their invitation

6.question: What did Nehemiah ask God amid the attempts to frighten him?
options: To strengthen his hands
To give him courage to face Sanballat
To reveal Tobiah's secret plans
To deliver him from Geshem's hands

6.question: Why was Shemaiah hired against Nehemiah?
options: To frighten him and make him sin
To convince him to abandon rebuilding the wall
To publicly accuse him of treason against the king
To take his place as governor of the province

6.question: What did Tobiah do through his letters?
options: He sought to put Nehemiah in fear
He asked Nehemiah's forgiveness
He offered timber for the wall
He invited Nehemiah to a feast

7.title: A faithful man
7.text: Nehemiah entrusts Jerusalem to Hanani and Hananiah, chosen because he was a faithful man who feared God above many. Character, not competence alone, qualifies for leadership.

7.question: What was the city of Jerusalem like at that time?
options: Large and great, but with few people in it
Narrow and walled, full of prosperous residents
Small and poor, but crowded with rebuilt houses
Surrounded by very high, strong walls

7.question: How many were the children of Shephatiah?
options: Three hundred seventy and two
Two thousand a hundred seventy and two
Six hundred fifty and two
A thousand two hundred fifty and four

7.question: How many were the children of Zaccai?
options: Seven hundred and threescore
Eight hundred forty and five
Six hundred forty and eight
Six hundred twenty and eight

7.question: How many were the children of Bigvai?
options: Two thousand threescore and seven
Six hundred threescore and seven
Six hundred fifty and five
Ninety and eight

7.question: How many were the children of Hariph?
options: An hundred and twelve
Ninety and five
Three hundred twenty and eight
Three hundred twenty and four

7.question: How many were the men of Kirjath-jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth?
options: Seven hundred forty and three
Eight hundred sixty and seven
Nine hundred forty and five men
Four hundred thirty and one

7.question: How many were the children of the other Elam?
options: A thousand two hundred fifty and four
A thousand three hundred twenty and one men
Nine hundred eighty and two men counted
Seven hundred fifteen men in all

7.question: To which group did the children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, belong?
options: The priests
The Levites
The singers
The porters

7.question: Who were the children of Asaph?
options: The singers
The porters
The Nethinims
The priests

7.question: To which group did the children of Hanan, Giddel, and Gahar belong?
options: The Nethinims
The gatekeepers
The servants of Solomon
The common people

7.question: Whose were the children of Barkos, Sisera, and Tamah?
options: The Nethinims
Solomon's servants
The temple Levites
The temple scribes

7.question: How many in all were the Nethinims and the children of Solomon's servants?
options: Three hundred ninety and two
Forty and two thousand
Six thousand seven hundred and twenty
Seven thousand three hundred thirty and seven

7.question: What did the Tirshatha say to those who could not find their register?
options: That they should not eat the most holy things until a priest stood with Urim and Thummim
That they should return to Babylon until the dispute over their lineage was fully resolved
That they should be cast out of the city until they proved their descent to the priests
That they should pay a fine to the governor for lacking genealogical records

7.question: How many camels were among those who returned?
options: Four hundred thirty and five
Seven hundred thirty and six
Two hundred forty and five
Six thousand seven hundred and twenty

7.question: Where did the priests, Levites, porters, and singers dwell?
options: In their cities
Only in Jerusalem
In Babylon
Outside the walls

8.title: The joy of the Lord is your strength
8.text: On hearing the law the people weep; but Nehemiah and the Levites comfort them: this day is holy, eat and share, for the joy of the Lord is your strength. Repentance flows into joy.

8.question: What did the people do when Ezra opened the book?
options: They stood up
They left the street
They began to sing
They went home

8.question: Why did the people weep when they heard the words of the law?
options: They were moved as they heard the law of God
They feared the enemies who threatened to attack the city
They were hungry because there was not enough food
They did not understand the language in which the law was read

8.question: What did they find written in the law?
options: That the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month
That they should rebuild the temple before celebrating the solemn feast of the booths together
That they should choose a king to rule over all the people of Israel that had gathered together
That they should pay tribute to the king of Persia every year required

8.question: For how many days was the book of the law read and the feast kept?
options: Seven days, with a solemn assembly on the eighth
Twenty-one days, without any additional assembly
Fifteen days, with continuous fasting and prayer
Three days, without any special celebration

9.title: Thou art Lord alone
9.text: The great prayer begins by acknowledging the Creator: Thou art Lord alone, who made heaven, earth, and the seas, and preservest them all. Israel's confession starts with who God is.

9.question: What did the Levites ask the people at the start of the prayer?
options: To bless the Lord for ever and ever
To fast forty days before the altar of the Lord
To rebuild the walls of the city before dawn
To offer sacrifices of atonement on the altar

9.question: What did God do against Pharaoh and the Egyptians?
options: He showed signs and wonders
He sent them prophets
He made a covenant with them
He gave them the promised land

9.question: How does the prayer describe God amid the people's rebellion?
options: Ready to pardon, gracious and merciful, slow to anger
Demanding immediate sacrifices to forgive the sins of the people
Judging the people with burning anger and without any mercy
Abandoning his people entirely to their own fate

9.question: How did God sustain Israel forty years in the wilderness?
options: They lacked nothing; their clothes waxed not old
Sent angels to fight against their enemies in the wilderness
Rained fire from heaven to destroy their adversaries
Multiplied their flocks and their riches

9.question: How did the people respond to God's goodness, according to the prayer?
options: They rebelled and slew the prophets who testified against them
They offered daily sacrifices and obeyed all of the commandments
They built new altars and temples to worship only the true Lord
They sent abundant offerings of gold and silver to the temple

9.question: Why did God not destroy or forsake the people?
options: For his great mercies' sake
Because the people were righteous
Because the enemies were weak
Because the king interceded

9.question: What did the people decide to do at the end of the prayer?
options: Make a sure covenant, written and sealed
Appoint a new high priest for the temple
Rebuild the walls of the city completely
Choose a new king to rule over Israel

10.title: Who sealed the covenant
10.text: At the head of those who sealed the covenant stands Nehemiah the governor. The leader does not ask of the people what he does not first take on himself.

10.question: To which group did Harim, Meremoth, and Obadiah belong?
options: The priests
The Levites
The chief of the people
The porters

10.question: Who were Shebaniah, Hodijah, Kelita, and Hanan?
options: Levites
Priests
Chief of the people
Singers

10.question: To which group did Bunni, Azgad, and Bebai belong?
options: The chief of the people
The descendants of the servants of Solomon
The heads of the families of the exiles
The singers of the temple

10.question: Who were Magpiash, Meshullam, and Hezir?
options: Chief of the people
Singers of the temple
Descendants of the Nethinims
Servants of the king

10.question: To which group did Malluch, Harim, and Baanah belong?
options: The chief of the people
The gatekeepers of the temple
The descendants of the Nethinims
The servants of the king

10.question: What did the people pledge concerning the sabbath?
options: Not to buy ware on the sabbath day
To harvest crops throughout the entire sabbath day
To sell foreign goods freely on the sabbath day
To open the city gates on the sabbath

10.question: What did the people promise to bring year by year to the house of the Lord?
options: The firstfruits of the ground and of all fruit trees
Armed soldiers to defend and protect the house of the Lord
Gold and silver taken from the defeated enemies of war
Captives from the neighboring conquered nations

10.question: What is the people's final pledge in this chapter?
options: Not to forsake the house of our God
To choose a new king to rule the people
To completely rebuild the walls of the sacred city
To return to live in Babylon

11.title: One of every ten
11.text: To repopulate Jerusalem, lots were cast to bring one of every ten to dwell in the holy city. Those who willingly offered themselves were blessed by the people.

11.question: From whom did Maaseiah, of those who dwelt in Jerusalem, descend?
options: From Baruch, of the sons of Shiloni
From Col-hozeh, of the sons of Joiarib
From Zechariah, of the sons of Amariah
From Joiarib, of the temple servants

11.question: What office did Joel the son of Zichri hold in Jerusalem?
options: Overseer over the men of Benjamin
Chief of the porters at the city gates
Overseer of the second part of the city
Chief of the house of God in the temple

11.question: Who was the overseer of the mighty men of valour?
options: Zabdiel, the son of one of the great men
Amashai, the son of Azareel, of the priests
Pedaiah, the son of Kolaiah, of Benjamin
Sallu, the son of Meshullam, of Benjamin

11.question: How many were the Levites in the holy city?
options: Two hundred fourscore and four
An hundred seventy and two
Four hundred threescore and eight
Eight hundred twenty and two

11.question: What was the king's commandment concerning the singers?
options: A certain portion for them, due every day
A certain portion of silver for the priests
The building of a new temple in Jerusalem
The keeping of the gates by the Levites

11.question: How far did the children of Judah dwell?
options: From Beer-sheba unto the valley of Hinnom
From the city of Dan unto the border of Beer-sheba
From Jerusalem unto the great river Euphrates
From mount Zion unto Bethel

11.question: Where were some of the Levites?
options: In divisions in Judah and in Benjamin
In divisions in Ephraim and in Manasseh
In the environs of Samaria and the city of Shechem
In the region of Moab and of Ammon, to the east

12.title: The dedication of the walls
12.text: For the dedication of the walls, they sought the Levites out of all places, to keep the feast with gladness, with thanksgivings and singing, with cymbals, psalteries, and harps.

12.question: In whose days did these chief of the priests serve?
options: In the days of Jeshua
In the days of David
In the days of Moses
In the days of Solomon

12.question: Whom did Joiada beget, according to the genealogy?
options: Jonathan
Eliashib
Jaddua
Joiakim

12.question: Who represented the house of Iddo among the priests?
options: Zechariah
Meshullam
Johanan
Adna

12.question: Who represented the house of Hilkiah?
options: Hashabiah
Nethaneel
Kallai
Uzzi

12.question: What office did Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, and others hold?
options: They were porters keeping the ward at the gates
They were singers, responsible for praise in the temple
They were priests, in charge of the daily sacrifices
They were guards of the royal palace, in the king's time

12.question: What did the priests and Levites do before the dedication?
options: They purified themselves and the people, the gates, and the wall
They offered sacrifices of atonement upon the altar of the temple
They completely rebuilt the gates and the walls of the city again
They called all the people to fast before the temple

12.question: With what did the brethren of Zechariah go, with Ezra before them?
options: With the musical instruments of David
With the silver trumpets of the priests
With banners and flags of their tribes
With offerings of grain and wine

12.question: What did the singers do at the dedication?
options: They sang loud, with Jezrahiah their overseer
They blew trumpets, with Zechariah leading them all
They danced in the streets, with the princes of Judah before them
They offered incense, with Ezra directing them

12.question: What did all Israel give in the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah?
options: The portions of the singers and the porters
The offerings for the daily sacrifices of the temple
The tithes for the maintenance of the priests
The firstfruits of the yearly harvest

13.title: Remember me, O my God
13.text: Throughout his reforms Nehemiah repeats a simple prayer: remember me, O my God, for good. His strength came not from the praise of men, but from God.

13.question: What had Eliashib prepared for Tobiah in the house of God?
options: A great chamber in the courts of the temple
A secret chamber beside the priests' courtyard
A guest house for the visiting foreign ambassadors
A storehouse for the temple's grain

13.question: What did Nehemiah command after casting out Tobiah's stuff?
options: To cleanse the chambers and bring back the vessels of God's house
To rebuild the destroyed altar and offer new sacrifices once again
To appoint new priests and Levites to serve in the restored temple
To gather all the people to rebuild the city's broken walls

13.question: What prayer does Nehemiah make as he restores the Levites' tithes?
options: Remember me, O my God, and wipe not out my good deeds
Grant me the victory over all my enemies, O Lord my God
Establish my throne forever in the land of Judah, O Lord my God
Send fire from heaven to destroy all my adversaries

13.question: What did Nehemiah do to keep the sabbath?
options: He commanded the gates to be shut before the sabbath
He opened the market for trading inside the city walls
He allowed the merchants to sell freely on the sabbath
He authorized the sale of fish in the city

13.question: How did Nehemiah react to those who married foreign wives?
options: He contended with them, cursed them, and made them swear by God
He rewarded them generously with fertile lands and royal honors
He appointed them leaders of the people and priests of the temple
He completely ignored the matter and went on his way

13.question: What is Nehemiah's final prayer in the book?
options: Remember me, O my God, for good
Make me king of Judah and the neighboring nations
Destroy the enemies who rise up against me
Give me great riches and many lands
